title: Numbers and Place Value
objectives: Understand the structure of numbers and the base-10 system
Read, write, and compare whole numbers up to 1,000,000
Recognize place values from units to millions
Round numbers to specified place values

introduction.context: Understanding large numbers is essential in everyday life - from reading population statistics and distances to managing finances and understanding measurements. Place value helps us make sense of numbers and perform calculations accurately.
introduction.connection: This chapter builds on basic counting skills and number recognition that you already have, extending them to larger numbers and more sophisticated comparisons.

concepts.title: The Base-10 Number System
concepts.content: Our number system is based on groups of 10. Each position in a number represents a different power of 10. Moving from right to left, each position is 10 times larger than the previous one.

concepts.title: Place Value Positions
concepts.content: Each digit in a number has a specific place value: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, and millions. The value of a digit depends on its position.

concepts.title: Expanded Form
concepts.content: Expanded form shows the value of each digit in a number. It helps us understand what each digit contributes to the total value of the number.

concepts.title: Comparing Numbers
concepts.content: To compare numbers, start from the leftmost digit and compare place by place. The first position where digits differ determines which number is larger.

steps: Identify the place value of each digit
Add all the place values together
commonErrors: Forgetting to include zeros in place values
Misidentifying which place value a digit occupies

steps: Line up the numbers by place value
Compare from left to right: ten thousands place - both have 1
Tens place - first number has 4, second has 5
commonErrors: Comparing from right to left instead of left to right
Not aligning numbers properly by place value

steps: Look at the digit to the right (hundreds place): 6
Increase the thousands digit by 1: 5 becomes 6
Replace all digits to the right with zeros: 6,000
commonErrors: Looking at the wrong digit to determine rounding
Rounding down when the digit is 5 or greater
Forgetting to change all digits to the right to zero

practice.problem: What is the value of the digit 7 in the number 3,742?
hints: Look at the position of the digit 7 in the number
Count the place values from right to left: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands
The 7 is in the third position from the right
practice.explanation: The digit 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 7 × 100 = 700.

hints: Break down each digit by its place value
2 is in ten thousands, 3 is in thousands, 4 is in hundreds, 5 is in tens, 6 is in ones
Multiply each digit by its place value: 2×10,000, 3×1,000, 4×100, 5×10, 6×1
practice.explanation: 23,456 = 20,000 + 3,000 + 400 + 50 + 6. Each digit is multiplied by its place value.

hints: Compare the numbers digit by digit from left to right
The first three digits are the same: 4, 5, 6
Look at the tens place: 7 vs 8
practice.explanation: 45,687 is larger because when comparing digit by digit, 8 > 7 in the tens place.

hints: Look at the digit to the right (tens place): 5
practice.explanation: The hundreds digit is 4, and the tens digit is 5. Since 5 ≥ 5, we round up to 8,500.

practice.problem: In the number 567,890, what digit is in the ten thousands place?
hints: Count place values from right to left
Ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands
The ten thousands place is the 5th position from the right
practice.explanation: Counting from right to left: 0 (ones), 9 (tens), 8 (hundreds), 7 (thousands), 6 (ten thousands). So 6 is in the ten thousands place.
